summary: Mahakachchakodiye Pangngasekara works in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Sri Jayewardenepura (2020–2023) and served as Senior Lecturer II at Bhiksu University of Sri Lanka from 2020 to 2024.

Mahala Rethlake specializes in Indology and religious studies. A doctoral candidate at the University of Chicago (attested 2026), she is affiliated with the university's PhD program in Religious Studies (Philosophy of Religions) through 2026.
Mahananda Timilsina is an Indologist who completed a PhD at Nepal Sanskrit University by 2015 and subsequently held an academic post there.

Maharshi Vyas is an Indology and religious studies scholar who was a PhD student at the University of California from 2017 to 2025. In 2025, he became an Assistant Professor at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill.

Mahasi Sayadaw (1904–1982) was a Buddhist studies and religious figure who studied under Mingun Jetawun Sayadaw U Narada, Aletawya Sayadaw, and Thelon Sayadaw. He served as abbot of Taung-waing-galay Taik Kyaung and resident teacher at Mahasi Sasana Yeiktha.
Mahaveer H. Muhammad works in history, archaeology, linguistics, and Indology. He earned an M.A. from Shah Abdul Latif University and has served as a researcher for the Government of Sindh.

Mahendradatta Jayadi is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA in Buddhist Studies from the International Buddhist College (2010–2013) and a Diploma in Pali from Somaiya Vidyavihar University (2022–2023).

Mahendranath Gupta (1854–1932) studied at Hare School, Presidency University, and the University of Calcutta. Active in religious studies and Indology, he held posts at Ripon College and Surendranath College around 1886 to 1900.

Mahesh A. Deokar works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at Savitribai Phule Pune University (1996–2002), became Head there in 2006, and serves as a Regional Representative for the Pali Text Society (attested 2026).

Mahesh Chandra Nyayaratna Bhattacharyya (1836–1906) was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Edward Byles Cowell. He served as Principal of Sanskrit College and University, with affiliations attested in 1882, 1894, and 1914.
Mahesh Kumar specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a BA Hons at Banaras Hindu University (2015–2020) and became a Research Scholar there in 2021.
Mahesh Raj Pant (born 1944) is an Indologist and historian who held posts at Samshodhana Mandala (attested 1982) and the University of Hamburg (attested 2001).

Mahinda Deegalle studied at the University of Peradeniya, Harvard, and the University of Chicago (PhD 1995). Active in Buddhist and religious studies, he held positions at Bath Spa University, Cambridge, Colgate, McGill, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
Mahiro Ito (born 1968) is a Buddhist studies scholar who has held professorships at Bukkyo University and Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026). He succeeded Norihiko Tanaka in 2021.

Maho Iuchi specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. After earning a PhD from Otani University by 2008, she served as a guest researcher at Kobe City University of Foreign Studies (attested 2010).
Mai Mishiro is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 2011) and Waseda University (attested 2016).

Makio Takemura (born 1948) studied at the University of Tokyo. Specializing in Buddhist studies and philosophy, he was a professor at the University of Tsukuba (~1989–2002) and president of Toyo University (2009–2020).

Makio Ueno completed a PhD at Otani University by 2009. Working in Buddhist studies and Indology, he held appointments at the Shin Buddhist Comprehensive Research Institute, Otani University, and Otani Academic Society.

Makoto Funaoka (born 1946) is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and history. He studied at Meiji University (~1965–1977) and served at Hokkai-Gakuen University (1993–2017), alongside part-time lecturing at Komazawa University and The Open University of Japan.
Makoto Fushimi is an Indologist who studied under Michio Yano and Michael Witzel. He held an affiliation at Harvard University (attested 2000).
